groups.name: write_throughput
groups.note: Bulk insert of N fresh keys into an empty engine, then one flush. Covers open, memtable inserts and the flush that writes the table. Both engines compress blocks on 4 threads.

groups.name: overwrite
groups.note: Every key written a second time into an engine that already holds one copy, then one flush. Memtable churn over existing keys and a superseding flush. Both engines compress blocks on 4 threads. ours-deferred-wal: our engine with a caller-kept log, the batch written to the log in one call and synced once, then the keys put in the memtable. rocksdb-wal: RocksDB writing the same batch through its own log with a sync. SurrealKV's commit does the same work. None of the three flushes in the timed window. ours-deferred-wal is set against rocksdb-wal, the plain arms and SurrealKV against RocksDB.

groups.name: overwrite_sustained
groups.note: 100,000 keys, then 15 rewrites of a hot set of 20,000 of them, with compaction behind the writes and a reader alongside. 4 MiB memtables, 2 MiB tables, 4 L0 runs per compaction, no write-ahead log on either. Ours flushes on a thread of its own as RocksDB does, one sealed memtable at a time as RocksDB's two write buffers allow, with deferred durability and one sync barrier per 8 flushes; it runs leveled compaction on another thread and stops writes at 36 L0 runs, RocksDB's stop trigger. Time per write; beside it the compaction bytes per written byte until compaction rests, the disk bytes over live bytes when the last write lands, and the reader's p50 and p99.

groups.name: overwrite_skew
groups.note: 200,000 writes into a memtable that already holds 100,000 keys, timed without a flush: the insert path alone. No write-ahead log on either; RocksDB's write buffer holds every write. Keys drawn in increasing order past the held set (append), uniformly from it, by Zipf(0.99) over it, or one key every time (hot). _w<N>: on N writer threads, 8-byte keys. _prefix<N>: one writer, keys behind an N-byte shared prefix.

groups.name: concurrent_mixed
groups.note:
Both engines hold 100,000 flushed keys; T threads run 200,000 operations on keys drawn by Zipf(0.99) over them, each a read with probability P% and an overwrite otherwise. _r

_t: P = 95 (YCSB-B) or 50 (YCSB-A), T = 32, 64 or 128. No write-ahead log on either and no flush in the timed window; RocksDB's write buffer holds every write. Time per operation across all threads.

groups.name: point_read
groups.note: One get per stored key on a warm engine. ours is the library default: each tree chooses, from its own reads, the share of its keys that goes through the row cache. ours-row-cache-on sends every key through it, ours-row-cache-off keeps no rows. Also our hash index and ribbon locator and RocksDB's hash index, measured with no rows, on the same chart.

groups.name: point_read_uniform
groups.note: As many gets as there are keys on a warm engine, each of a key drawn evenly from all of them, at 70,000 and 1,000,000 keys through the 16 MiB cache. ours chooses its row cache share, ours-row-cache-on sends every key through the row cache, ours-row-cache-off keeps no rows.

groups.name: point_read_zipf
groups.note: As point_read_uniform, the keys drawn by Zipf(0.99).

groups.name: point_read_hot
groups.note: As point_read_uniform, nine draws in ten from a hundredth of the keys and the tenth from any.

groups.name: point_read_phase
groups.note: As point_read_uniform, the first half of every pass drawn as point_read_hot and the second half evenly: the reads change under the cache twice a pass.

groups.name: point_read_cold
groups.note: One get per stored key on an engine opened on a fresh copy of the state, its files dropped from the OS page cache and its block cache empty. Only the reads are timed, each on its own; beside the mean, their p50 and p99.

groups.name: multi_get
groups.note: One batched lookup of the whole key set on a warm engine (RocksDB: batched_multi_get_cf). The groups of 1 and 4 MiB values give both engines a 128 MiB block cache, above the 64 MiB one batch reads: at 16 MiB RocksDB's HyperClockCache kept a batch's blocks past its capacity (64 MiB measured) while ours admitted none of them, so the group compared two cache policies and not two batched reads.

groups.name: range_scan
groups.note: A full forward scan reading every value on a warm engine.

groups.name: seek_random
groups.note: A seek to each key in scattered order, reading the value under the cursor.

groups.name: major_compact_zstd3
groups.note: Six overlapping L0 tables merged into one level, 4-thread block compression, no range split. zstd level 3, the level RocksDB applies to bottommost output.

groups.name: subcompaction_zstd3
groups.note: A full overwrite in six L0 tables merged into a bottom level of several tables, split into 4 parallel ranges. High-entropy values. zstd level 3.

rocksdb: 16 MiB HyperClockCache, Ribbon filter at 10 bits per key, optimize_filters_for_hits, async_io reads, io_uring on Linux
